newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - April 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - April 30.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Wednesday:
* The Dow Jones industrial average posted its second biggest point gain ever, ending up 179.01 points at 6,962.03 after a U.S. economic report reduced inflation concerns.
* The Employment Cost Index showed no inflation signals despite a strong U.S. economy and signs that skilled workers have become harder to find.
* PepsiCo earnings were higher than expected, helped by strong profits at its Frito-Lay snack business and good results in its domestic beverage operations.
* Oracle Chairman Larry Ellison said despite earlier indications of interest, he had decided to put off buying troubled Apple Computer for the moment.
* The U.S. government told employers they could not discriminate against qualified workers with mental illness nor could they ask job applicants if they had a history of mental illness.
* Marvel Entertainment bondholders, led by Carl Icahn, proposed a bankruptcy restructuring plan for the company which would give Marvel's trading card businesses to bank lenders.
* Airlines are reporting an increase in unruly behavior aboard planes from passengers who are banned from smoking, crammed into seats and given alcohol.
* Market place: Money now going into equity mutual funds is now more likely to be bound for overseas rather than domestic equities.
* Freeport-McMoran Copper and Gold chief executive James Moffett said unless tests of the Busang gold site in Indonesia yielded sufficient metal, the company would pull out of developing the field.
* IBM announced a share buyback plan, a 14 percent dividend boost and a stock split approval, pushing its shares higher.
* Legal and political opposition have cast doubts on the awaited privatisation of giant Brazilian state-owned mining company Vale do Rio Doce.
* An academic center and three companies said they were forming a research group to study human genome research with the hopes of identifying possible new drugs and treatments.
* High tolls have caused the Suez Canal to lose business.

* Advertising: The commercials aired during a controversial series of a U.S. television show in which the main character announces she is a lesbian are likely to get as much attention as the show itself.
